resources.string: Prefer a dedicated keyboard? Enable the Nemotron Voice Input keyboard, then switch to it from your keyboard switcher when you want voice input as its own keyboard.

Nemotron speech streaming 0.6B (English) runs entirely on-device and streams text live while you speak. The model (~700 MB) is downloaded once on first launch; after that no audio ever leaves your device and no network is used.

How to use it
• Open any app and tap the microphone on a supported keyboard/app. A small panel slides up, you speak, tap to stop, and the text is inserted. (Enable “Auto-stop after silence” in the settings to have it stop by itself.)

Which keyboards open the voice panel
• Microsoft SwiftKey (not open source) and website voice search open the panel directly.
• AnySoftKeyboard is the open-source way to get the panel: its mic key opens it as long as no voice keyboard is enabled on your system.

Other open-source keyboards
• HeliBoard, FlorisBoard, OpenBoard, Fossify Keyboard and Unexpected Keyboard don't open the panel: their mic key switches to the “Nemotron Voice Input” keyboard instead. Enable it once (see “Alternative: Voice keyboard”), speak there, and use its keyboard-switch key to go back. FUTO Keyboard ships its own voice input.
• Gboard only uses Google's own voice typing and can't use this app at all.

If SwiftKey's own voice typing opens instead
• Settings → Rich input → turn off “Multi-modal voice typing”.
• Then tap the mic again and pick “Nemotron Voice Input”.

If Android asks which app to use
• Choose “Nemotron Voice Input” and tap “Always”.

If another app always opens instead
• Open Settings → Apps → that app → “Open by default” → Clear defaults, then try again.
